moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- customer lock-in: deep, repeat relationships with marquee PSU and private clients — evidence: named relationships with SAIL, IOCL and JSW Steel supporting revenue visibility and repeat order flow
- technology: expertise in Zero Liquid Discharge, advanced membrane-based treatment and energy recovery from wastewater differentiates the company — evidence: cited as core expertise areas in the Chairperson's letter and MD&A — against it: emerging competitive interest from established players such as WABAG and Thermax in the high-purity water treatment segment for data centres

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Contracts run 12 to 36 months in tenure, and geopolitical and labour-supply disruptions have, on occasion, delayed dispatches.
- Concentration in a limited number of large contracts, including the ₹313 crore JSW order, and in the steel and oil & gas end-markets.
- The anticipated ZMD patent grant, targeted for July 2027, faces timeline risk given the extended, multi-jurisdictional nature of the filing process.
- Inflation in metals, electrical components, fuel and civil materials, only partly mitigated through price escalation clauses in customer contracts.
- Established players such as WABAG and Thermax are showing emerging competitive interest in the high-purity water treatment segment for data centres.
- The Secretarial Audit Report notes the database did not fully capture all instances of sharing Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI) in real time, and the list of designated persons was incomplete.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Disciplined execution of a growing order book
- Expanding the annuity-like operations & maintenance (O&M) portfolio
- Continued investment in proprietary technology
- Selective bidding rather than broad bidding to protect margins
- Selective international expansion in African and European markets
- Migration to the NSE/BSE main board on completion of the mandatory three-year SME tenure
